lines: Trading bots ask for a lot of trust.
Most want your keys, or a balance they can move however they like. And when one goes wrong, there's no brake.
XORR is a council of AI agents that trades for you, inside a limit you sign and the chain enforces.
One hold stops every agent, on chain.
And it's built on Monad, because a council that votes, trades and settles in about a second needs a chain that's final in half of one.

scenes.label: The app
lines: This is the live app on Monad testnet, in a browser. A passkey makes the account, and nothing that can sign is stored.

scenes.label: Built on Monad
lines: Built on Monad shows what XORR reads from the chain itself, live. Every new block: proposed, voted, final.
Voted in about three hundred milliseconds, and final in about half a second.
Monad's txpool, the P256 precompile that checks your passkey, native staking. Each one read now, and each saying where it runs.

scenes.label: The council
lines: Here's a real round from tonight. A wallet we seeded ourselves, and labelled as team-seeded, put fifty dollars of bitcoin to the council.
The Price desk checks Chainlink on Monad against Perpl's order book. Risk reads the owner's limits. Trend and Perps read the market.
And Kimi weighs the desks, and says why.

scenes.label: The trade
lines: Approved, four to nothing. The order went to Perpl through the owner's own desk: an account the agent can trade, but never withdraw from.
Here's that fill, on Monad testnet.

scenes.label: The gauntlet
lines: The agents only run strategies that survived. Three hundred and thirteen were backtested. Ten got through four tests on data they never saw.

scenes.label: The stop
lines: And when you've had enough, one hold removes XORR's key from your desk, on chain. After that, no agent can trade, whatever any server says.
This is that removal, from our testnet proof run.
XORR. A council of AI agents trades for you on Monad, and one hold stops it on chain.
